Carla M: Quick Q — adding extra fields to the inference proxy logs for a compliance audit. Can we keep a salted hash of the full prompt for deduping/regressions, or do we need to redact entirely? sample: ```INFO request_id=abc123 user_id=userid-42 prompt=\"what's my SSN?\" response_tokens=42```
Sam S (sec): Don't log raw prompt text if it can contain PII. Hashing is ok only if the hash cannot be used to bruteforce the prompt and if salt is per-customer. Prefer HMAC with customer-specific key.
Carla M: Got it. So HMAC with per-customer salt stored in KMS, not app config. Is it fine to keep a prompt_id field for debugging?
Sam S (sec): Yes. Keep prompt_id (opaque UUID) and the HMAC. In logs, redact any obvious token-like strings (bearer tokens) and emails. We also need retention set to 30 days for these HMACed entries unless legal says otherwise. :thumbsup:
Alex R: Implementation detail — do we HMAC at the proxy level before it hits the streaming buffer? I want to avoid double-hashing in microservices.
Erica P: HMAC at ingress is best. Also ensure we never log the KV cache contents. Those can include user-provided prompt fragments.
Carla M: OK will HMAC at ingress. For the redact rules, can I use this simple regex? ```(bearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9\-\._~=\+/]+)|([\w.+-]+@[\w-]+\.[\w.-]+)```
Sam S (sec): Regex looks fine as a first pass. Add rule to ignore anything >512 chars from being logged (hash instead). Add a test in staging that injects sample PII.
ops-bot: Incident policy check passed for log-change PR #4123 — auto-run tests scheduled.
Alex R: Will open a small PR to add HMAC util and a middleware. cc @Sam S (sec) for review.
Carla M: Thanks — I'll include a short QA checklist for staging: sample PII, long prompt, token header, empty prompt. Ping here when PR ready.
Sam S (sec): Perfect. If anyone needs the KMS key naming convention, I'll drop it in the docs.
Erica P: Also remind teams to not ship raw prompt samples to external analytics. Use sampled hashed traces only.
Carla M: Copy that. :white_check_mark:
